newsitem.title: UK: BBC extends short wave radio broadcasts to Albania.
newsitem.headline: BBC extends short wave radio broadcasts to Albania.

text.p: The British Broadcasting Corporation said on Monday it was extending its short wave radio broadcasts to Albania following the closure of its FM transmitter there.
The transmitter on Mount Dajti in central Albania was switched off on Sunday after the declaration of a state of emergency thoughout the country, the BBC said in a statement.
The BBC said more than half the adult population of Albania are regular listeners to its Albanian-language broadcasts.

"In the current situation everyone is desperate for news and it is vital that Albanians know they can turn to the BBC to find out what is happening in their country," said Tim Cooke, head of the BBC Albanian service.
Listeners on short wave were being urged to tell friends and relations that the BBC was still on the air.

From Monday there will be three daily short wave transmissions to Albania from Britain and Cyprus. In addition to the usual broadcasts at 0630 and 1800 GMT, the 1415 GMT programme will be switched from FM to short wave.
In its statement, the BBC rejected allegations by the Albanian ambassador to London, Pavli Qesku, who said BBC had incited violence in southern Albania.
"At all times we have sought to avoid anything which might aggravate an already tense situation," said Andrew Taussig, Director of BBC World Service Regions.
Armed unrest has flared in southern Albania and police have threatened to shoot stone-throwers on sight.
Widespread protests have erupted since thousands of Albanians lost their life savings when pyramid investment schemes collapsed.
